newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislature misses budget deadline.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislature misses budget deadline.

text.p: Both houses of the California legislature recessed on Monday without passing a budget for the start of the 1997-1998 fiscal year on July 1.
"There's not going to be a budget ... before the July 1 deadline," said Ron Gray, spokesman for Assembly Speaker Cruz Bustamante.
"I don't think anybody expected it to get done on time," Sandy Harrison, spokesman for Senate President Bill Lockyer, added.
Leaders of the Senate and Assembly, and the state's budget conference committee said welfare reform was the major stumbling block.
"The welfare issues are going to need to be resolved before there's a vote on the budget," Lockyer told reporters.
Gov. Pete Wilson's office called on legislators to finalize the budget immediately, but officials said negotiations were likely to stretch on for another week.
The legislature's budget conference committee -- made up of three senators and three assembly members -- has been holding daily hearings on the state's key fiscal issues.
The committee's goal was to meld the budget packages of the Assembly and Senate into a single spending plan for the fiscal year that begins July 1.
The conference committee has already missed the state's Constitutional budget deadline of June 15.
Senator Mike Thompson, who chairs the committee, said he hoped the panel would conclude its work on the budget on Wednesday.
The final budget was expected to be in the $67 billion to $70 billion range.
